page: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a fractional GPU instance within the Cloud GPU family. It features 8 shared vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel x86_64 cores running at 2.0 GHz, with a cache configuration of 32 KB L1d, 4 MB L2, and 16 MB L3. System memory consists of 40.0 GB of RAM, providing 5.0 GB per core. The instance includes a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with a 0.3333 allocation, delivering 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided via a 740 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard CPU and memory operations, alongside top-tier performance in specific machine learning workloads. The stress-ng single-core score is 1786.68, and the multi-core score is 14175.12. Passmark CPU and memory scores are 14090.9 and 2190.35, respectively. In LLM inference tests using a small 135M model, the instance achieves top-tier results with 9944.32 tokens per second for prompt processing and 464.42 tokens per second for text generation. For a medium 7B model, prompt processing reaches 3147.67 tokens per second and text generation reaches 107.73 tokens per second.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is its shared CPU allocation and fractional GPU configuration, which may introduce resource contention compared to dedicated hardware. However, the fractional GPU model offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring GPU acceleration without the expense of a full physical GPU. This resource density makes it suitable for small-to-medium LLM inference, machine learning development, database operations, and static web serving.
